meta.description: Cumulative NERSA-registered generation capacity in South Africa since 2018. Source: SAPVIA NERSA Registered Plants Dashboard (lookerstudio.google.com/reporting/a7de0801-10c7-4610-8689-3a281e823ac1). Data collated by SAPVIA Grid Access Working Group from NERSA quarterly media statements.
meta.note: Cumulative total since registration regime began in 2018. Updated to Q1 2026/27 (Apr-Jun 2026): NERSA registered 124 facilities totalling 804 MW, of which 122 solar PV at 236 MW and 2 wind at 568 MW. Cumulative since 2018 is 2,619 facilities and 20,131 MW, about R409bn invested. Average investment cost in the quarter was R25,099/kW. Northern Cape took the largest share at R11.934bn for 440 MW.
meta.licence_note: Licence covers this compilation - the assembly, correction and structuring of the underlying data. Source data remains under its own terms; see the source field.
meta.cumulative_discrepancy: TWO CUMULATIVE TOTALS EXIST AND THEY DISAGREE. This file carries SAPVIA's collation: 2,619 facilities, 20,131 MW, ~R409bn. NERSA's own Q1 2026/27 statement gives 2,692 facilities, 21.9 GW and R452.9bn — a gap of 73 facilities and about 1,769 MW. The QUARTERLY figures agree exactly (124 facilities, 804 MW, R20.2bn), so the divergence is in the accumulated history, not the latest period. NOT RECONCILED. Do not average them and do not silently switch: quote the SAPVIA figure with its source, or NERSA's with its own, and say which. The likeliest explanation is a different treatment of deregistered or superseded facilities, but that is inference. Ask SAPVIA or check a NERSA quarterly directly.
meta.tracking_caveat: NERSA HAS NO MECHANISM TO TRACK WHICH REGISTERED PROJECTS GET BUILT, and no legislated deadline requires a developer to build a registered plant (NERSA, Q1 2026/27). So this is a PIPELINE OF INTENT, not a build record. Separately, embedded generation under 100 kW needs no NERSA registration at all and most of it is registered with neither Eskom Distribution nor municipalities, so the total is an UNDERCOUNT of small plant and an OVERCOUNT of what will exist.

quarters.note: Two wind projects carried 71% of the capacity across 124 registrations. Northern Cape took the largest investment share at R11.934bn for 440 MW.
